rules.title: Security deposit capped at one month's rent
rules.requirement: For residential rentals, a landlord may not demand or receive security, however denominated, of more than one month's rent, in addition to the first month's rent. Exceptions apply for advance rent on leases of six months or longer, tenant-requested alterations, and qualifying small landlords.
rules.quoted_span: Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.
rules.coverage_text: Security for a rental agreement for residential property that is used as the dwelling of the tenant.
rules.exemptions: Advance payment of at least six months' rent on a lease of six months or longer. Mutually agreed fees for tenant-requested alterations. Small landlords under (c)(5) may take up to two months' rent. Does not apply to security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024.
rules.penalty: Bad faith claim or retention of security may subject the landlord to statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages.
rules.conflict_note: The section note says it was amended effective January 1, 2026 (AB 414). The cap itself applies to security collected or demanded on or after July 1, 2024, per (c)(6).

rules.title: Small landlord exception: two months' rent
rules.requirement: A landlord who is a natural person (or an LLC whose members are all natural persons) and who owns no more than two residential rental properties with no more than four units in total may take security of up to two months' rent. This exception does not apply when the prospective tenant is a service member.
rules.quoted_span: Notwithstanding paragraph (1), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to two months’ rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy if the landlord meets both of the following requirements:
rules.coverage_text: Landlords who are natural persons (including family trust settlors and beneficiaries) or LLCs with all natural-person members, owning no more than two residential rental properties with no more than four dwelling units offered for rent.
rules.exemptions: Not available if the prospective tenant is a service member. The landlord may not refuse to rent to a service member because of this limit.
rules.penalty: Statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security for bad faith retention, plus actual damages.

rules.title: Higher security charged to service members: written statement and return
rules.requirement: If a landlord charges a service member higher-than-standard security based on credit or housing history, the landlord must give a written explanation by the lease signing. The extra amount must be returned after no more than six months of residency if the tenant is not in arrears.
rules.key_value: Return of extra security within 6 months
rules.quoted_span: (4) On or after April 1, 2025, if a landlord or its agent charges a service member who rents residential property in which the service member will reside a higher than standard or advertised security pursuant to paragraph (1) due to the credit history, credit score, housing history, or other factor related to the tenant, the landlord shall provide the tenant with a written statement, on or before the date the lease is signed, of the amount of the higher security and an explanation why the higher security amount is being charged.
rules.coverage_text: Service members (as defined in Military and Veterans Code § 400) renting residential property in which they will reside.

rules.title: Photographs of unit required for deposit deductions
rules.requirement: The landlord must photograph the unit after possession is returned and before repairs or cleaning, and again after those are completed. For tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025, the landlord must also photograph the unit at move-in, and the photos must accompany any deductions.
rules.key_value: Move-out photos from 2025-04-01; move-in photos for tenancies from 2025-07-01
rules.quoted_span: (2) Beginning April 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after the possession of the unit is returned to the landlord, but prior to any repairs or cleanings for which the landlord will make a deduction from or claim against the security deposit pursuant to this section, and shall also take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after such repairs or cleanings are completed.
rules.coverage_text: Residential tenancies subject to Civil Code § 1950.5.
rules.penalty: Landlord is not entitled to claim any security if it fails in bad faith to comply with subdivision (h). Statutory damages of up to twice the security for bad faith retention.
rules.conflict_note: Move-in photograph requirement applies to tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025 (subdivision (g)(1)).
